archetype.name: Dual-Threat (scramble-first)
archetype.definition: An undrafted rookie whose value came from breaking the pocket and running, not from designed runs, while his passing stayed short, cautious and turnover-prone whenever the ball had to travel.

report.headline: Spot starter whose legs worked, but whose arm lost him the job.
report.take:
Jalon Daniels is a 24-year-old undrafted rookie who started Weeks 4 through 6 for Tampa Bay, went 1-2, and is back to QB2 behind Baker Mayfield, who started Weeks 7 and 8. His card should be read as a three-start audition on a team built to win around its quarterback. The Buccaneers' defense ranks 2nd in EPA, the run game ranks 7th, and the offense passes 7 points less often than situation predicts. The staff asked him to manage games. As a starter he averaged 167 passing yards and threw 4 interceptions in those three starts.

The passing profile is stark. He threw short: 5.23 intended air yards, and his average throw landed 4.15 yards short of the sticks. Even there he was below expectation, with a -6.2 CPOE on 0-9 yard throws. The 10-19 yard window was a disaster: 26.3% completions, a -29 CPOE and 2 interceptions on 19 attempts. His 18.4% bad-throw rate ranks 36th of 38. The damage concentrated where it hurt most. His within-one-score dropbacks added up to -19.3 EPA, and close fourth quarters ran -0.612 per play with 3 interceptions. The Pittsburgh start (-21.8 passing EPA, 5 sacks, 26.8% bad throws) is effectively why his season line looks the way it does.

What the numbers hide is that the non-passing game was genuinely useful. He scrambled on 13% of dropbacks, those scrambles were worth 0.451 EPA apiece with 7 first downs, and his 0.321 rush EPA per carry is strong. The 9 deep attempts (1.036 EPA per play) and 9 red-zone plays with 3 TDs look good, but they are handfuls of snaps, not traits. One oddity: his targets to Emeka Egbuka returned -15.3 EPA, while Ted Hurst, Cade Otton and Chris Godwin were all positive. That looks more like a timing or forcing problem with one receiver than a talent verdict on either player.

Going forward, he is a backup with no career baseline to lean on. If he plays again, expect the same shape: useful scrambles, sacks, checkdowns and an interception rate the league will not tolerate from a starter.

strengths.title: Scrambles that move the chains
strengths.body: He left the pocket on 13% of dropbacks, and those plays were his most efficient offense, averaging 0.451 EPA with 7 first downs. It is a real skill that tends to travel: improvisation under pressure is what kept drives alive when the passing game stalled. His rushing yardage ranks 11th among qualifiers despite only three starts.

strengths.title: Occasional shot plays landed
strengths.body: On 9 throws of 20+ air yards he posted 1.036 EPA per play and a +10.9 CPOE. That is the one passing area where he beat expectation, and it hints at arm talent the short game didn't show. Nine attempts with an interception mixed in is a hint, not a strength to bank on.

strengths.title: Clean in the red zone
strengths.body: All 3 of his touchdown passes came in 9 red-zone plays, with no turnovers there and 0.412 EPA per play. The condensed field shortens his reads, which suits a quarterback who struggled to process the middle depths. The sample is too small to project.

concerns.title: Intermediate window is broken
concerns.body: Throws of 10-19 air yards produced a 26.3% completion rate, a -29 CPOE and 2 interceptions, the core of a 5.11 YPA that ranks 45th of 47. This is the zone that demands anticipation and throwing into windows. His conservative air-yards-to-sticks number suggests he knew it. Without a career record it reads as a rookie processing flaw rather than bad luck.

concerns.title: Turnovers when games tighten
concerns.body: His 5.1% interception rate ranks 45th, and the giveaways clustered in leverage. Close fourth quarters ran -0.612 EPA per play with a 40.9% completion rate and 3 interceptions. On a team whose defense keeps nearly every game within one score, that is the costliest place a quarterback can fail. It is a big part of why Mayfield is back under center.

concerns.title: Sacks and scattershot accuracy
concerns.body: A third of his pressures became sacks, and his 18.4% bad-throw rate ranks near the bottom of the charted group. Some of the sack rate is the price of a scrambler hunting space. But the scrambles did not offset the drive-killers in the Pittsburgh start (5 sacks, -21.8 passing EPA). Short-area inaccuracy plus sacks makes the offense live behind the chains.

trend.note: Three starts swung from -4.3 passing EPA against Green Bay to +5.9 against Dallas (the 32nd-ranked defense) to -21.8 against Pittsburgh. After that he returned to a 10% snap cameo in Week 7, and he has no logged action since Mayfield reclaimed the job.

nextGame.headline: Backup role at Chicago; a relief appearance would face a strong pass rush.
nextGame.body:
Daniels is QB2, so he only matters at Chicago if something happens to Mayfield or the game gets out of hand. If he does play, the Bears are a poor fit for his weak spots. They rank 2nd in sack rate, which feeds his 33% pressure-to-sack habit. They are 4th against short passes, where nearly all of his throws live. Their one glaring hole is deep EPA allowed (dead last), and the only passing zone where he was efficient was deep. That is a narrow path on a tiny sample.

On availability, Egbuka (foot) is listed out with an estimated return on game day, so his status is uncertain. Daniels' targets to him went badly anyway, and he moved the ball better toward Hurst and Otton. For Chicago, cornerback Malik Muhammad (75% of snaps) and edge Grady Jarrett (72%) carry injury designations with game-day return estimates. Their absence would soften both the coverage and the rush he would face. Tampa Bay is a 6-point underdog with a 46.5 total, a script that could mean more dropbacks for whoever is at quarterback.

keyMatchups.title: Bears pass rush vs. his sack habit
keyMatchups.body: Chicago gets home at the 2nd-best sack rate in the league. Daniels turned a third of his pressures into sacks. Any relief snaps likely include drive-ending sacks unless he gets out on scrambles.

keyMatchups.title: Deep vulnerability vs. his shot plays
keyMatchups.body: The Bears allow the most EPA on deep passes, and his 9 deep attempts were his best throws. It is the one passing matchup that leans his way, though the sample is thin.

keyMatchups.title: Short-area squeeze
keyMatchups.body: Chicago ranks 4th against short throws, and 70 of his 98 attempts traveled under 10 air yards at -0.125 EPA. The checkdown offense he ran as a starter would have little room here.

nextGame.watch: Whether Mayfield finishes the game healthy; Daniels only enters the picture if he doesn't.

restOfSeason.body:
The base case is a backup's season: near-zero snaps, maybe a cameo in a blowout or a series if Mayfield is banged up. If he is pressed into a start, expect what the three-game audition showed, roughly 140-190 passing yards with real rushing value from scrambles. Expect sacks and an interception rate that should come down from 5.1% simply because few quarterbacks stay that high, though not to league average. The red-zone touchdown efficiency and the deep-ball EPA rest on 9 plays each and should regress. The scrambling is the part most likely to hold.

With no career history behind him, everything here is a three-start read on an undrafted rookie. Any growth in the intermediate window would be the real tell that he is more than an emergency option.

confidence.note: 98 attempts, three starts, no career baseline, now a backup.
